@PPLXDevs The traditional tool-calling approach suffers from high latency, manual control flow, and context pollution.

With Search as Code, the model composes search primitives: fanning out queries asynchronously, deduping, filtering, joining, and ranking before results hits its context. https://t.co/4cLyvDIFXi
@perplexity_ai @PPLXDevs The interesting shift is treating search less like a single answer box and more like a small program that can gather, filter, and rank before the model spends context.
@perplexity_ai @PPLXDevs search as code sounds like overengineering when a simple curl works, but i'll try it with my custom script

@perplexity_ai @PPLXDevs The long-term trend is clear:

Models are becoming decision-makers.
Code is becoming the execution layer.

Agents are becoming the bridge between the two.
@perplexity_ai @PPLXDevs just tried to implement search as code and ended up generating a thousand lines of junk. who else wants to hug their codebase and cry?

@perplexity_ai @PPLXDevs @perplexity_ai Search as Code inverts the agent architecture debate. I've been waiting for retrieval to become a testable, version-controlled module rather than a hardwired prompt layer - this is that shift, and it makes agentic workflows meaningfully more composable.
@perplexity_ai @PPLXDevs writing python instead of chaining tool calls is clever. is the bigger win lower latency, or just fewer dead-end loops?

This is a bigger deal than it looks.
Before this your agent asks a question, waits for results, then figures out what to do. Now the search logic lives inside the code. The agent just runs it.
Less back and forth. Faster. Way less stuff that can go wrong in between.
Anyone plugged this into something live yet?

@perplexity_ai @PPLXDevs Latency isn't from the loop — it's from the round-trip overhead on each tool call. Generating Python doesn't reduce HTTP calls, it just shifts parsing from JSON to AST. Same rate limits, same error recovery, harder to debug when the agent writes broken syntax.
@perplexity_ai @PPLXDevs this makes sense for latency. the part i’d want to see is debugging: when the generated search code is wrong, do users see the plan or just the answer?

@perplexity_ai @PPLXDevs This is so cool ! We explored a similar idea from the "deep search" side: open-source deep search with dynamic search graphs, open models, and API deployment. Fun to see the industry converging on search becoming programmable. https://t.co/GKwec3sTNw
@perplexity_ai @PPLXDevs writing python to handle search calls instead of manual loops is a pretty big shift, excited to try this out

@perplexity_ai @PPLXDevs This will turn out to be a game changer... no latency,  not much surfing the outputs least advertising ( even if someone later starts somehow)
Good job.
@perplexity_ai @PPLXDevs "Search as code" makes a ton of sense. Writing custom Python pipelines beats hammering sequential API loops every single time.

the code-as-search-plan pattern is genuinely underrated. most frameworks keep the search pipeline implicit inside a serial tool loop. generating python means one plan step instead of N round trips, and the strategy is inspectable + deterministic. the failure mode i'd watch is iterative search where a mid-result changes your next move. wide fan-out works, re-planning mid-pipeline is the hard part

@perplexity_ai @PPLXDevs Most search APIs hand you results.

Search as Code hands you a program. Interesting.
@perplexity_ai @PPLXDevs @grok detailed thread on research and application sources so I can hand off to Claude workflow swarm
@perplexity_ai @PPLXDevs if you want to do this in your agents use DSPy and read the RLM paper or just use the open source ax library ax-agent https://t.co/y45nH1PCrQ

Wooow, I implemented something like this in my product about half a year ago.

Except it wasn’t just about search - it applied to tool calling in general.

The reason is intuitive: there is far more data on writing code than on tool calling.

(Although you still need to provide some guardrails, like max_char_num or retries)

@perplexity_ai @PPLXDevs This is the right abstraction I think. Tool calling was always too stiff for research workflows; once the agent can write little search programs, the harness stops looking like a vending machine.

@perplexity_ai @PPLXDevs Right call killing the tool-call loop. Eight sequential search calls is eight round-trips of pure model overhead; one Python block collapses that to a single committed plan. Latency math sells it.
@perplexity_ai @PPLXDevs hey @grok is this the same thing as @Cloudflare code mode?
@perplexity_ai @PPLXDevs Search as Code makes agents faster and their code simpler. 🚀🐍
@perplexity_ai @PPLXDevs a solid architectural evolution for ai agents. single turn code execution should drastically reduce overhead.

@perplexity_ai @PPLXDevs Why wouldn't a dedicated search api with all of the de-dup and ranking optimized by you guys be better than my model having to figure out how to do it myself?

What's the advantage to having more fine grain control?

the shift from tool-calling to code generation for search is the same pattern we're seeing everywhere. tool calling is the training wheels. code generation is the real interface. instead of the model asking permission to search one thing at a time, it writes a program that fans out 20 queries in parallel, dedupes, filters, and ranks before results even hit the context window. the model stopped being a search user and became a search engineer. 0.871 on DSQA at half the cost of anthropic's approach tells you the architecture matters more than the model underneath it.
@perplexity_ai @PPLXDevs software reduces to primitives so that more software can be generated to be run

interesting trend:

browser harness: don't overbuild browser-use, just ask model to generate script on the fly

search-as-code: don't build the perfect search, let model/agent define how to retrieve/rank

use token to replace one-size-fit-all infra

agent gets smarter and everything else gets more primitive.
@perplexity_ai @PPLXDevs future of search
@perplexity_ai @PPLXDevs Amazing progress! Faster, smarter, and more scalable agents. 🚀
@perplexity_ai @PPLXDevs Search as Code is a smart shift letting AI agents execute search through code instead of chained tool calls unlocks faster, more scalable reasoning. 🚀
